```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```r
library(BFS)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf) # install.packages("sf")
```

## Base maps

`bfs_get_base_maps()` returns the
[cartographic base maps](https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/regional-statistics/base-maps/cartographic-bases.html)
of the BFS ThemaKart project as sf objects. The first call downloads the
base maps (a zip file of several hundred files) and caches them;
`bfs_clear_cache()` deletes the cache.

```r
switzerland <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "suis")
cantons <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "kant")
districts <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "bezk")
communes <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "polg")
capitals <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "stkt", type = "Pnts", category = "kk")
lakes <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "seen", category = "11")
rivers <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "flus", category = "22", type = "") # rivers have no type

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = communes, fill = "snow", color = "grey45") +
  geom_sf(data = lakes, fill = "lightblue2", color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = districts, fill = "transparent", color = "grey65") +
  geom_sf(data = cantons, fill = "transparent", color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = rivers, color = "lightblue2", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = capitals, shape = 18, size = 3) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(caption = "Source: ThemaKart, © BFS")
```

<p align="center" class="screenshot"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgnbhl/BFS/master/man/figures/base_maps.png" alt="Map of Switzerland with its communes, districts, cantons, lakes, rivers and cantonal capitals" width="700"></p>

### Choose a file

Each file name combines the arguments of `bfs_get_base_maps()`, e.g.
`K4kant20220101gf_ch2007Poly.shp`: geometry `kant`, date `20220101`, category
`gf` (total area), type `Poly`, format `shp`.

<p align="center" class="screenshot"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgnbhl/BFS/master/man/figures/base_maps_file.png" alt="Structure of a ThemaKart file name" width="600"></p>

By default you get the most recent file; use `date` for another date of
validity, e.g. `date = "20230101"`. With `return_sf = FALSE` you get the
file path instead of an sf object. An argument set to `""` matches any
value, so to list all the river files:

```r
bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "flus", category = "", type = "", date = "", return_sf = FALSE)
```

The default `asset_number` is the 2024 edition of ThemaKart. Pass another
asset number for another edition, e.g. `"11927607"` for 2020.

### Interactive maps

```r
library(mapview)

bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "bezk") |>
  mapview(zcol = "name", legend = FALSE)
```

<p align="center" class="screenshot"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgnbhl/BFS/master/man/figures/mapview.png" alt="Interactive map of the Swiss districts" width="700"></p>

### Join statistics

The communes have their BFS number in the `id` column. Join it with the
commune register included in the package (`register_gde`) or with any BFS
dataset by commune:

```r
communes_ge <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "polg", date = "20230101") |>
  inner_join(filter(register_gde, GDEKT == "GE"), by = c("id" = "GDENR"))

lake_leman <- bfs_get_base_maps(geom = "seen", category = "11") |>
  filter(name == "Lac Léman")

bbox_ge <- st_bbox(communes_ge)

ggplot(communes_ge) +
  geom_sf(data = lake_leman, fill = "lightblue2", color = "grey65") +
  geom_sf(fill = "snow", color = "grey65") +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = name), size = 3, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  coord_sf(xlim = bbox_ge[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bbox_ge[c("ymin", "ymax")]) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Communes du canton de Genève", caption = "Source: ThemaKart, © BFS")
```

<p align="center" class="screenshot"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgnbhl/BFS/master/man/figures/base_maps_ge.png" alt="Map of the communes of the canton of Geneva" width="700"></p>

For the communes at another date, or their history (mergers, renamings),
see the [swissMunicipalities](https://github.com/SwissStatsR/swissMunicipalities)
package.

## Geodata of the Swiss geo-portal

The [Swiss geo-portal](https://data.geo.admin.ch/) publishes the geodata of
the BFS and other federal offices in a STAC API. `bfs_get_catalog_geodata()`
lists its collections. With their metadata, it sends one request per
collection and takes a few minutes, so save the result:

```r
catalog_geodata <- bfs_get_catalog_geodata()

catalog_geodata |>
  filter(grepl("^ch.bfs", collection_id)) |>
  select(collection_id, title)
```

Download the files of a collection with `bfs_download_geodata()` (requires
the rstac package). Zip files are not extracted:

```r
files <- bfs_download_geodata(
  collection_id = "ch.bfs.generalisierte-grenzen_agglomerationen_g1",
  output_dir = "borders_g1"
)
files
```

Some layers are also available as a Web Map Service (WMS), e.g. with leaflet:

```r
library(leaflet)

leaflet() |>
  setView(lng = 8, lat = 46.8, zoom = 8) |>
  addWMSTiles(
    baseUrl = "https://wms.geo.admin.ch/?",
    layers = "ch.bfs.generalisierte-grenzen_agglomerationen_g2",
    options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", transparent = TRUE),
    attribution = "Generalised borders G2 © BFS"
  )
```

<p align="center" class="screenshot"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgnbhl/BFS/master/man/figures/leaflet_g1.png" alt="Leaflet map with the generalised borders of the BFS" width="700"></p>

The use of the geodata is free but subject to the
[terms of use](https://www.geo.admin.ch/terms-of-use) of the Swiss geo-portal.
